subject: Hosted API renewal & commit top-up — AtlasRetail
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API renewal & commit top-up — AtlasRetail

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a concise renewal proposal that includes a stepped monthly commit increase and a soft-burst cushion to cover seasonal peaks. Summary below and proposal attached.

Key points:
- Current monthly hosted commit: 2M tokens -> Proposed: 3.5M tokens (+75% monthly commit)
- Tiered rate bands: preserved at current per-token rate for first 3.5M, then a reduced overage rate that is still lower than on-demand pricing
- Soft-burst window: up to 20% additional capacity for high-traffic windows (subject to a 10% usage smoothing policy)
- Operational guardrails: automatic prefix caching for storefront flows, request-level throttles during sustained bursts, and a 24/7 escalation path.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Review attached PDF (AtlasRetail_commit_proposal_2027-08.pdf) — this includes the new payment schedule and SLO targets.
2) We confirm a start date for the upgraded commit (target week of Sep 6).
3) If procurement needs the updated contract, I can route DocuSign once we lock the numbers.

If you want, I can loop in Karthik for a short ops/throughput runbook review — he has suggestions for incremental throttles and cache configurations that keep latency under 200ms P95.

Cheers,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachment: AtlasRetail_commit_proposal_2027-08.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@atlasretail.com>

Date: 2027-08-14T11:05:00-07:00

Vanessa —

Thanks for the proposal and the quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions from our side before we escalate to legal/procurement: 

1) Can you confirm the behavior if we exceed the soft-burst window for two consecutive weeks? Is there an automatic throttle or will we be moved to on-demand?
2) For the tiered overage rate, can you show an example monthly spend for a high-growth scenario (+40% traffic month)?
3) Ops: we want the canary period for the new commit to include an increase to prefix cache TTLs rather than a full KV flush — is that planned?

Procurement is copied — once we have the answers we can share internally and decide on timelines. We are very keen on the Sep window but need a clear operational escalation path and a short-run observability checklist.

Thanks —
Laura Chen
Head of Product Operations, AtlasRetail
laura.chen@atlasretail.com

(On procurement: they will want the DocuSign-ready contract and an itemized billing schedule rather than a lump sum.)

Karthik / Ben —

Looping you both in. Laura from AtlasRetail had three operational questions (see below). Need a quick ops-runbook reply that I can forward back to Laura and procurement. High level asks: 1) behavior if soft-burst is exceeded two weeks in a row, 2) example spend on +40% growth, 3) canary plan re: prefix TTLs vs KV flush.

Context: we proposed a 3.5M monthly commit with a 20% soft-burst cushion and a reduced overage rate (proposal attached). They prefer a Sep start date. I want to keep the Sep 6 target but we should be explicit about throttles and fallback model (automatic graceful degradation -> version fallback -> on-demand only as last resort).

Please respond with:
- Short ops bullets I can paste into an email to procurement (2–4 bullets)
- Any changes to the commit start date you recommend based on provisioning lead time
- Whether we should recommend a partial Dedicated reservation for their peak weekends (brief cost/benefit note)

Thanks —
Vanessa

Vanessa / Ben / Laura —

Thanks for pulling this together, Vanessa. Quick operational answers and recommended language for procurement: 

- If soft-burst is exceeded for two consecutive weeks: we trigger the soft-usage review. Practical behavior: first sustained exceedance -> automatic 15% token-rate smoothing for peak prefixes for the remainder of that week, second consecutive exceedance -> temporary rate-limit gating per-route (not global) plus an account manager notification. We do NOT auto-migrate to full on-demand; on-demand is only used when both (a) customer exceeds gated thresholds and (b) customer explicitly requests overage settlement. This keeps traffic online while protecting SLOs.

- Example spend model (+40% traffic month): for a 3.5M commit, +40% equals 4.9M tokens. Pricing example we can paste to procurement: base commit covered: 3.5M @ current rate; overage: 1.4M @ overage rate = X cents/token (see attached PDF for exact numbers). On average this scenario increases monthly spend by ~28% vs current commit spend. (We can produce a line-item spreadsheet if procurement wants exact figures.)

- Canary ops plan (prefix TTLs vs KV flush): recommended approach: incrementally increase prefix cache TTLs during the canary (24–72 hours) and monitor 95th latency and error rate thresholds. Avoid full KV flushes unless we see consistent cache thrash. I attached a compact ops playbook for AtlasRetail with step-by-step checks and a scaling_matrix for throttles.

Recommendations for the go-live date:
- Provisioning lead time: 7–10 business days to finalize commit allocation and set up the soft-burst policy in control plane.
- If they want Sep 6 start, we should sign by Aug 26 to meet internal ops lead times.

Dedicated suggestion: given their weekend peak patterns, recommend a small Dedicated reservation for two high-traffic weekends each quarter rather than full Dedicated. This reduces cost vs full reservation and provides a predictable buffer. I can include a cost delta table if procurement asks.

Language for procurement (copyable):
- "Redwood will apply a 20% soft-burst window on top of the committed monthly tokens. If soft-burst usage is sustained for more than one consecutive week, Redwood will apply progressive per-route rate gating and initiate an account review. Overages will be billed at the agreed overage rate unless the customer elects to purchase additional committed capacity."

Attachments: redwood_ops_playbook_AtlasRetail.md (ops checklist), scaling_matrix_AtlasRetail.csv (throttle matrix)

Happy to refine numbers — ping me for a quick 15-min call if you want to run the model live.

—Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
